candidates.name: Andy Barr
candidates.background: U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 6th District since 2013; attorney and former deputy general counsel to Gov. Ernie Fletcher. Senior member of the House Financial Services Committee. Won the May 19 Republican primary with 64% over former Attorney General Daniel Cameron (28%), boosted by President Trump's endorsement; businessman Nate Morris dropped out May 1.
priorities: Secure the border and deport criminal illegal immigrants
Unleash American energy and bring back coal

cost.label: Bring back coal to 'lower energy costs'; opposed ESG mandates (campaign site)

health.label: Called the ACA 'this 2,700-page monstrosity'; backed the AHCA as 'patient-centered' with more 'competition and choice'; voted to repeal the individual mandate (Ballotpedia)

immigration.label: 'Deport all criminal illegals and secure the border': restart wall construction, reinstate Remain in Mexico, end catch-and-release; A+ from NumbersUSA (campaign site)

taxes.label: Voted for the 2025 'largest tax cut in American history' and pledges to 'cut taxes for every Kentuckian' (campaign site)

climate.label: 'No one fought Biden's war on energy more': bring back coal to lower energy costs, block ESG mandates, oppose the Green New Deal (campaign site)

safety.label: 'Strongly supports police': voted to increase federal law enforcement funding, championed the STOP Chinese Fentanyl Act; endorsed by the Kentucky FOP (campaign site)

repro.label: Voted for the Pain-Capable Unborn Child Protection Act, a 20-week abortion ban (Ballotpedia)

housing.label: Championed a 2026 housing package that 'slashes big government regulations to accelerate homebuilding' while also limiting institutional investors' home purchases (House office)

education.label: Cosponsored a school choice scholarship bill and 529 expansion so parents and teachers decide 'what is best for their education', alongside public career-tech funding (House office)

democracy.label: Voted for the SAVE Act voter ID mandate: 'Anyone who opposes voter ID to safeguard the integrity of our elections is anti-American' (House office)

candidates.name: Charles Booker
candidates.now: Former Kentucky state representative; founder of Hood to the Holler
candidates.background: Former Kentucky House member (2019-2021), at the time the youngest Black state lawmaker in Kentucky, and founder of the nonprofit Hood to the Holler. Lost the 2020 Senate primary narrowly to Amy McGrath, won the 2022 nomination but lost to Rand Paul. Won the May 19 Democratic primary with 47% over McGrath (36%), running as an unapologetic progressive.
priorities: The 40x40x45 plan: 40-hour week, 40 hours paid sick leave, $45,000 minimum income
Housing as a human right with a Tenant Bill of Rights

cost.label: 40x40x45 plan: anyone working 40 hours gets 40 hours of paid sick leave and a $45,000 minimum income, made 'tax free' by a Cost of Living Tax Exemption (campaign site)

health.label: 'Healthcare is a human right': Medicare for All; Type 1 diabetic who rationed insulin (campaign site)

housing.label: 'Housing is a human right': Tenant Bill of Rights with just-cause eviction and right to counsel, build affordable housing (campaign site)

taxes.label: Wealth tax and equal tax rates on capital gains: 'wealth should be taxed the same as work' (campaign site)

education.label: 'Full and equitable investment in our education system'; tuition-free public colleges and student debt cancellation (campaign site)

safety.label: 'Decriminalizing poverty' and building community safety through holistic investment (campaign site)

repro.label: 'Abortion is healthcare': restore abortion rights, repeal the Hyde Amendment, full coverage for abortion and contraception (campaign site)

democracy.label: As a state representative sponsored House Bill 6 to automatically restore felon voting rights: 'Once you have completed your sentence... you should be able to have your voice heard again' (PBS NewsHour)
